outcome.acceptance: 5/6 substantively met, 1 superseded by the operator's G-8 decision

summary: Phase-8 aligned direct:a2ui to the real A2UI v1.0 protocol and delivered a working rendering host. The acceptance criteria were written before the G-8 decision and four assumed the local dialect that alignment superseded; each was judged on what it actually tested rather than as literally worded. Criterion 6 — rendering verified in a browser DOM rather than by string-matching — is MET, closing the equivalent of phase-7's only PARTIAL.
deltas_found: REFRAMING: A2UI is a real external protocol (a2ui-project/a2ui, 16,230 stars, Apache-2.0, ports to .NET/Swift/Android/React Native) and our schema was not it. Specs our refiner validated were not A2UI documents. Same defect class as phase-7's TOOL_CALL_ARGS_DELTA, one level up: a wrong document model rather than a wrong enum value, and larger because direct:a2ui shipped in PR #1.

The built-in JSON Schema validator implemented `oneOf` as `anyOf` (stopped at first match), so two-operation envelope messages validated cleanly. `not` and `anyOf` were unimplemented entirely, leaving every dialect guard and the expression guard silently inert. p8-01's envelope exclusivity existed on paper only until p8-02 fixed the validator.

The A2UI renderer could never render a conformant spec: three lowercase component cases against a schema mandating PascalCase — zero overlap. No HTML was ever produced; nothing substitutes the template's {{A2UI_JSON}} placeholders. Bindings were never resolved (grep count 0).
Two prompts/execute.md instructions directed executors to run an HTML injection step that does not exist in the repository. Corrected in p8-03.

The real catalog ships 18 components and contains no `Heading` — a name that appears in a type union. Both my mock and p8-03's shipped example used it; the renderer correctly reported `Unknown component: Heading` rather than degrading.
corrective_actions: Schema, normalizer, examples, and six referencing files migrated to the real protocol; the old dialect is now rejected by name ahead of generic schema errors.
Validator gained real oneOf, plus anyOf and not, so the guards actually run.
@a2ui/react + @a2ui/web_core adopted at exact pins rather than hand-writing a renderer — the prior hand-written switch is exactly what failed.
A negative fixture in the old dialect retained so the format cannot creep back unnoticed.
Feature-name derivation fixed to use to_kebab(), preventing a duplicate feature directory.

recommended_next: Fix the scaffold-react-vite-agui.sh feature-name bug before starting a new phase
recommendation_rationale: It is a known, diagnosed, one-line defect in shipped code producing a broken second feature directory in every AG-UI scaffold. The fix is already written for A2UI; porting it takes minutes. Leaving a known defect while starting new work is how the AG-UI enum drift survived a whole phase.
next_phase_precondition: VERIFY MCP-UI IS NOT ANOTHER A2UI. Twice now a local artifact has diverged from an external standard of the same name (AG-UI enum, A2UI document model). Before assessing phase-9, check whether MCP-UI has an upstream specification and whether anything in this repo already claims to implement it.
